payload.summary: The pinned repo (angus924/rocket @ 36bd908) is the official ROCKET code. The claim maps to code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py, which generates 10,000 random kernels (code/rocket_functions.py), transforms train/test with apply_kernels, fits RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True) on the fixed UCR _TRAIN/_TEST split, and records the mean test accuracy over num_runs (default 10) of re-drawn kernels. ECG200 is in the bake-off dataset list in .preprint/reproduce_experiments_bakeoff.py. The data is NOT bundled; it must be obtained from the UCR 2018 archive (txt version) and placed at {input_path}/ECG200/ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200_TEST.txt. No dependency manifest exists in the repo (no requirements.txt, pyproject, or lockfile); README lists Python, Numba, NumPy, and scikit-learn. Saved outputs for this dataset exist in results/results_ucr.csv and results/results_ucr_resamples.csv, but I have not used or reported those values as the result.

entrypoints.why: Official UCR experiment script; runs ROCKET with 10,000 kernels and RidgeClassifierCV over N runs (default 10) and reports mean test accuracy per dataset via score() on the fixed train/test split.
Kernel generation (generate_kernels) and transform (apply_kernels) implementing ROCKET features; Numba-jitted.
Alternate bake-off script (includes ECG200 in its dataset list) from the preprint folder; same method.

metricSources.description: Computes _results[i] = classifier.score(X_test_transform, Y_test) per run and stores the mean as accuracy_mean; written to results_ucr.csv. The mean across runs is the claimed metric.
Saved output table with a row for ECG200 (saved output; not used as the reproduced value).
Saved resample results with a row for ECG200 (saved output; not used as the reproduced value).

payload.runInstructions: 1) Acquire UCR 2018 txt archive and place ECG200 files as {input}/ECG200/ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200_TEST.txt. 2) Create a file ecg.txt containing the line ECG200. 3) From code/: python reproduce_experiments_ucr.py -d ecg.txt -i <input_parent> -o <output_dir> -n 10 -k 10000. 4) Read accuracy_mean from output_dir/results_ucr.csv. Environment: Python with numpy, pandas, numba, scikit-learn; no pinned versions in the repo. Note: RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=True) was removed in newer scikit-learn, so an older scikit-learn version may be required.

payload.summary: Plan to measure ROCKET (10,000 kernels, RidgeClassifierCV with alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True) on the fixed UCR ECG200 train/test split, mean test accuracy over 10 runs with re-drawn kernels, using the pinned repository's rocket_functions.py (commit 36bd908) via the reviewed single-dataset adapter rocket-ecg200-runner, which mirrors the loop in code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py. The official script itself is not run because it fails on a one-row dataset-name file and writes CSV rather than the JSON metric parser needs. The repository has no dependency manifest; the reviewed pinned requirements pass dependency_check for linux/arm64 on Python 3.11 with binary wheels. Dataset comes from the reviewed download with sha256 pinned, extracted to the lab path. Output is artifacts/result.json, read via metrics.accuracyMean. No seed is fixed (the upstream code uses unseeded numba np.random), so run-to-run variance is expected and is recorded as the per-run accuracies and population standard deviation.

supervisorProposal.rationale: The reproduction did not produce an observation. The plan's command ran ../work/adapter/rocket_ecg200_runner.py, which is neither the declared entry point (code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py) nor the reviewed adapter ID, so policy_review blocked it (policy_block brd_0da8cceab5574dba98e6cc0fd779572a). Preparing, executing and reviewing were all skipped, so no command ran and no metric was produced. The paper's claimed mean test accuracy (0.9272) therefore has no reproduced counterpart, and neither a match nor a mismatch can be inferred. The repository analysis, paper claim and dataset plan are sound as far as the board shows, but the blocked command is what determines the outcome. The status should stay inconclusive; a re-plan that routes execution through the declared entry point or a correctly registered adapter would be needed before the claim can be tested.
